## `client.principals`

The `principals` resource of the platform API.

### `client.principals.create`

Signature: `client.principals.create(name: str, type: str, *, override_reason: str | None = None) -> Principal`

Create a principal.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The principal's unique name. |
| `type` | `str` | required | `"USER"` or `"SERVICE_ACCOUNT"`. |
| `override_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Why, 10 to 500 characters on one line, to create a service account although an access file manages its scope (an audited override, for an administrator of the instance). |

Returns: `Principal`. The created principal.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a principal of this name already exists. |

### `client.principals.get`

Signature: `client.principals.get(name: str) -> Principal`

Fetch a principal by name.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The principal's name. |

Returns: `Principal`. The principal.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no principal of this name exists. |

### `client.principals.list`

Signature: `client.principals.list(*, search: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None, cursor: str | None = None, sort: str | None = None, order: str | None = None) -> list[Principal]`

List principals, newest first.

The principals of one page; `list_page` also returns the cursor of the next one, and `iter` walks every page.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | `str | None` | `None` | Only principals whose name contains this text, in any letter case. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most principals returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (100). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. Send the same `search` and sort with every page. |
| `sort` | `str | None` | `None` | The sort, as `list_page` takes it. |
| `order` | `str | None` | `None` | ``asc`` or ``desc``, as `list_page` takes it. |

Returns: `list of Principal`. Newest first.

### `client.principals.list_page`

Signature: `client.principals.list_page(*, search: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None, cursor: str | None = None, sort: str | None = None, order: str | None = None) -> PrincipalPage`

List one page of principals, newest first, with the cursor of the next page.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | `str | None` | `None` | Only principals whose name contains this text, in any letter case. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most principals returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (100). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. Send the same `search` and sort with every page. |
| `sort` | `str | None` | `None` | What the principals are sorted by: ``created`` (the default), ``name`` (in any letter case) or ``status``, the active first, each by name. |
| `order` | `str | None` | `None` | ``asc`` or ``desc``; by default ``desc`` for ``created``, ``asc`` for the others. |

Returns: `PrincipalPage`. The principals, and the cursor for the next page (`None` on the last).

### `client.principals.iter`

Signature: `client.principals.iter(*, search: str | None = None, page_size: int = 100, sort: str | None = None, order: str | None = None) -> Iterator[Principal]`

Yield every matching principal, newest first, fetching pages as needed.

|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | `str | None` | `None` | Only principals whose name contains this text, in any letter case. |

| `order` | `str | None` | `None` | ``asc`` or ``desc``, as `list_page` takes it. |

### `client.principals.permissions`

Signature: `client.principals.permissions(name: str, *, environment: str | None = None, namespace: str | None = None, table: str | None = None) -> Permissions`

Say what a principal may do on an object, action by action, and through which grant.

The answer comes from the authorizer the server's routes use. Without an object it is about the instance. Anyone may ask about themselves; asking about another principal needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The principal. |
| `environment` | `str | None` | `None` | The object's environment. |
| `namespace` | `str | None` | `None` | The object's dot-joined namespace (needs `environment`). |
| `table` | `str | None` | `None` | The object's table (needs `namespace` and `environment`). |

Returns: `Permissions`. One entry per action the server asks for on such an object.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | About another principal, without the `ADMIN` role on the instance. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | For an administrator: no such principal, environment, namespace or table. |

### `client.principals.grants`

Signature: `client.principals.grants(name: str) -> list[HeldGrant]`

List the live grants a principal holds, directly and through its groups.

Newest first, each with the name of the group it comes through (`None` for a direct grant). Anyone may ask about themselves, with a personal token or in the web interface; asking about another principal needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance, and a task or CI token may not ask even about its own principal.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The principal. |

Returns: `list of HeldGrant`. The grants; they say nothing about who made them.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | About another principal, or through a task or CI token, without the `ADMIN` role. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | For an administrator: no such principal. |

### `client.principals.deactivate`

Signature: `client.principals.deactivate(name: str, *, override_reason: str | None = None) -> None`

Deactivate a principal.

Sets `is_active = False` rather than deleting the principal, preserving every grant, PAT, and audit entry that references it.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The principal's name. |
| `override_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | To deactivate a service account although an access file manages its scope, in an emergency: why, 10 to 500 characters on one line. Needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance; audited, and the next apply reverts it unless the file lists it. |

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no principal of this name exists. |

### `client.principals.unlink_provider`

Signature: `client.principals.unlink_provider(name: str) -> None`

Unlink a person from the organisation's identity provider.

Deletes their stored passkeys, revokes all their personal API tokens, ends their sessions and withdraws their open sign-in links; they come back with a new recovery link. Needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance. To offboard someone, deactivate them instead.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The person's principal name. |

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no principal of this name exists. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | For yourself, or a person who is not linked. |
